$comment: Child-safe educational-content policy — version 1.0.0. READ docs/CHILD_SAFE_CONTENT_POLICY.md first.
One file, read by every gate: the Python import/dictionary/anchor builders (scripts/content/child_safety.py),
the TypeScript bank/cloze builder, the runtime delivery gate in apps/web, the release scanner
(scripts/content-safety-qa.mjs) and the packaged-artefact scanner. Two evaluators, one policy, and a
shared fixture file (packages/content-safety/fixtures/*.json) that both evaluators must pass.
Severity: HARD_BLOCK never reaches a learner on any surface, the dictionary included. CONTEXT_BLOCK is
refused on every random or generated surface (assessment options, distractors, gap-fills, recommendations)
and is allowed on a taught card or a dictionary row only when the item is named in `allow`. INTERNAL_ONLY
text may exist in policy documents and isolated test fixtures and never in a learner asset.
Match modes. `substring`: the compact form (Unicode-normalised, zero-width and punctuation removed,
spaces removed) contains the term — right for unambiguous multi-syllable Korean lexemes, and it is
what catches 섹스하다, 섹 스, 섹.스 and 섹스를. `token`: the term at a script-run boundary, optionally
followed by a Korean particle — for short terms whose syllables occur inside ordinary words. `headword`:
compared only against a headword or an answer choice, never inside running text (보지 마세요 is 보다).
`phrase`: whole-word sequence in a space-delimited language. `pattern`: an explicit regular expression.
`except` lists longer strings that contain a term and are safe; they are blanked before matching
(성교육 is sex education, 시발점 is a starting point, 노른자위 is a yolk). `allow.headwords` and
`allow.senseIds` name items a concept may not flag at all (성별 is glossed 'sex' and means gender).

categories.sexual: Sexual acts, slang, pornography, anatomy used sexually, sex work, sexual violence, sexualised description.
categories.political: Parties, politicians, elections as campaigns, slogans, ideologies, protest, disputes, contested territory, current conflicts.
categories.profanity: Profanity, obscenity, masked and abbreviated profanity, slurs, degrading insults.
categories.drugs: Illegal drugs, drug use and trade, substance-abuse slang, casual intoxication.
categories.gambling: Betting, casinos, wagering, gambling venues and slang.
categories.violence: Murder, assault, weapons, bombs, graphic injury, kidnapping, torture, trafficking, war.
categories.self_harm: Suicide and self-harm terminology, methods, ideation, encouragement.
categories.mortality: Death-centred wording that is not violent. CONTEXT_BLOCK: kept only on named daily-life cards.

latinScript_comment: The interface languages written in the Latin alphabet. A Latin-letter word inside a field of any other language (Korean, Japanese, Arabic, Hindi…) is foreign there, and is read against the English lists as well as its own; in these languages every word is Latin, and only the language's own lists apply — German 'die' is an article, not the English verb.

concepts.guidance: Neutral civic vocabulary stays (정치, 대통령, 선거, 투표하다, 국회). Replace a partisan, campaign, slogan, ideology or dispute item with a neutral civic or geographic sentence at the same level; a card whose taught sense is the partisan term is retired.

contextRules.why: 총 is a total (총 세 개) and a gun; only the weapon frame is blocked.
칼 peels an apple; the stabbing frame is blocked.
A person or animal in the object slot of a violent predicate.
약 is medicine; only the misuse frame is blocked.
보지 마세요 is 보다; 보지를 is the anatomical term.
년 and 놈 as counters or in 이 년 동안 are ordinary; with a demonstrative or an insulting modifier they are insults.
A person dying is mortality even when the verb is ordinary; a plant or a phone dying is not.

glossIndicators._comment: English gloss fragments that classify a dictionary or corpus entry into a category regardless of its Korean surface. Substring on the lower-cased gloss, after `except` strings are blanked. Deliberately narrow: a gloss indicator removes a dictionary row, so 'army' and 'police' are not here and 'rape' is.

except: as of an arm, leg, wing, sword

allow._comment: Strings that must never be flagged whatever the concepts say. `exact` is compared against a whole field after normalisation; `headwords` against a headword or answer choice; `senseIds` against a card's taught sense.
